transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Product), Sofia Patel (CTO, Greenfield), Dr. Evan Moore (Head of ML), Lydia Barnes (Security Lead), Tommy Ruiz (Infra)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-week pilot focused on inference of genomic annotation models with specific security gates (SOC 2 / ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS) and benchmark acceptance criteria (p50/p95 latency, throughput at target QPS, memory footprint). Customer emphasized PHI/PII handling (HIPAA implications) and EU data residency for cross-border samples.

Topics covered:
- Pilot success criteria and acceptance tests
- Workload sizing: qps, concurrency, dataset composition
- Benchmark matrix: latency/throughput, failure/DR tests
- Security + compliance: SOC 2 artifacts, SSO integration, RBAC model, audit logging + SIEM ingest, KMS/HSM key management
- Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC / on-prem considerations
- Timeline and next steps

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros — we'll scope the pilot and nail down what you need to sign off.
[00:18] Sofia: Thanks — we're trying to move faster but security gating is non-negotiable, we can't expose raw genomic PHI to a public multi-tenant service.
[00:30] Lydia: yeah, SOC 2 plus HIPAA controls matter. We also need audit logs shipped to our Splunk instance, and SSO (SAML) for everything.
[00:45] Diego: Totally — we typically run a pilot with either Redwood Hosted behind a customer-configured VPC peering layer or Redwood Private deployed into a customer VPC / on-prem. For anything with PHI we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
[01:02] Tommy: For infra, peering is fine as long as certs and firewall rules are ironed out. Question: does Redwood support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) HSM?
[01:15] Priya: Yes — KMS integrations are supported. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and we also provide envelope encryption for stored artifacts. We'll share the KMS integration matrix.
[01:33] Dr. Evan: On the benchmarks, we need to validate both long-context models (20k tokens) and short inference (<=512 tokens). Our production target is 10 qps for short calls and 2 concurrent long-context requests. p95 latency targets: short calls < 120ms, long calls < 1.2s.
[01:55] Diego: Good detail — we'll design a benchmark harness. Out of the gate for the pilot we should aim to reproduce p50/p95 numbers and token throughput. Our bench will measure cold-start, warm-cache, and sustained load for 30 minutes at target QPS.
[02:12] Sofia: Can you simulate the KV cache behavior? We rely heavily on prefix caching.
[02:19] Diego: Yep, we'll include KV cache warm vs cold scenarios. We'll also provide a script to replay customer traces if you share a sample (anonymized).

[02:40] Lydia: Audit logs — we need append-only records, user IDs (SAML subject), model version, request/response hashes, token counts, and per-request latency. Also flagged content alerts for PII/PHI detection.
[02:58] Diego: Redwood can stream audit logs to customer SIEM using syslog/HTTPS. We can include request/response metadata (not full responses by default). For PHI-sensitive responses, we can redact or hash payloads — that is configurable.
[03:20] Lydia: That hashing approach works if we can later correlate hashes to full content under controlled circumstances.
[03:28] Maya: Noted — we'll document our retention and redaction options.

[03:45] Sofia: On compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates? And what scope do they cover?
[03:55] Priya: We have SOC 2 Type II covering our platform services, and ISO27001 for our information security program. We'll attach the scoping matrix; note that for Private deployments some controls fall under customer responsibility (network controls, IAM).
[04:18] Sofia: Ok, we need the artifacts for legal review — SCP, SOC 2 report, encryption attestations.

[04:30] Diego: Regarding SSO integration — SAML is supported. We map identity to RBAC roles. We'll need an IdP metadata file from you and a list of RBAC roles we should create (viewer, dev, infra-admin, audit-only).
[04:47] Tommy: For RBAC, we want least privilege, and the ability to restrict model rollouts to a small group. Also API keys must be revocable and tied to users.
[04:57] Diego: Keys are revocable; we can also enable short-lived tokens and IP allowlists for endpoints. For pilot, we'll demo role scoping and key revocation.

[05:15] Dr. Evan: Timelines — we have a board review in 4 weeks. Can we run a 2-week pilot with benchmarks and a short compliance review to present?
[05:25] Maya: Yes — typical pilot timeline: week 0 prepping artifacts and dataset/samples, week 1 run bench and integrate SSO + audit streams, week 2 validate results and assemble acceptance report. That's compressed but doable if artifacts are shared quickly.
[05:42] Sofia: If we aim for a 2-week bench, we need Redwood to commit to a specific test matrix and acceptance criteria now so legal can see it.
[05:51] Priya: We'll propose a concrete acceptance checklist: p50/p95 latency thresholds, throughput sustainability test (30m), no data exfil in logs, SSO SAML integration passing with at least 2 RBAC roles, audit stream delivered to your SIEM, KMS BYOK proof-of-concept.

[06:10] Lydia: On data residency — some samples must remain within EU. Can you scope a region-specific deployment?
[06:18] Diego: Absolutely — Redwood can pin deployment regionally for Hosted or run Private in your EU VPC. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity in eu-west-1. We'll indicate where model weights and logs are stored per configuration.

[06:34] Sofia: Cost question — long-context ops with 20k tokens blow up cost; how do you recommend balancing latency and unit cost?
[06:43] Maya: It's the usual tradeoff. For the pilot we'll show both quantized model variants and batching strategies. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching profiles to hit your cost target while keeping p95 within limits. Dedicated capacity gives better unit cost predictability than Hosted burst.
[07:02] Dr. Evan: Can you run quantized runs during the bench so we can see quality delta vs latency?
[07:08] Diego: Yep — we'll run full-precision and 4-bit runs and include quality metrics (exact match, precision/recall on our eval set).

[07:25] Tommy: For networking, we'll need a runbook: firewall rules, subnets, peering, and certificate thumbprints.
[07:32] Maya: We'll share a prep doc with the runbook and a checklist of what to configure.

[07:45] Sofia: Legal will want to see indemnification, data handling SOPs. Can we have Redwood's DPA and standard security addendum?
[07:53] Priya: Yes — we'll attach our DPA and the pilot SOW template.

[08:05] Lydia: A detail on audit logs — retention windows, TTLs, and ability to export raw logs for forensic analysis. We also want to ensure log encryption at rest and in transit.
[08:18] Diego: Logs are encrypted in transit; at rest they follow the storage knee with customer KMS for Private. Retention is configurable; we'll show the defaults and how to export.

[08:33] Sofia: What about model version pinning for the pilot so we can reproduce results?
[08:39] Diego: You can pin model version/weights and we will include that in the acceptance report with hashes. Rollbacks are supported.

[09:01] (several minutes of technical back-and-forth between Diego and Dr. Evan about sequence lengths, memory footprints, kv cache sizing — transcript paraphrased below)
[09:01] Dr. Evan: For the long runs, we expect 20k context with a KV cache sized ~30GB per instance. We target 2 concurrency across 4 instances for scale.
[09:20] Diego: That maps to ~240GB RAM across instances plus GPU memory. We'll propose instance types and a cost estimate in the bench proposal.
[09:36] Diego: Also we'll test autoscaling thresholds and can simulate node failures for graceful degradation.

[09:55] Sofia: Acceptance criteria recap?
[10:00] Maya: 1) Bench: reproduce p50/p95 for short and long contexts within +/- 10% of target; 2) Security: SOC 2 artifact reviewed, SAML SSO integrated, RBAC roles implemented, audit stream validated in your SIEM; 3) Data handling: BYOK/HSM proof and residency enforced; 4) Operational: Runbook + run of failover test; 5) Documentation + SOW signed for next phase.

[10:30] Lydia: We'll add a gating item: no persistent plaintext of PHI in logs during pilot.
[10:38] Diego: Agreed — default redact; we'll only include hashes unless you explicitly allow full payloads under controlled export.

[10:50] Sofia: Who owns post-pilot performance regressions? We need a rollback and SLA commitment if we move to production.
[10:58] Maya: For pilot we'll provide performance baselines. Production SLAs are part of Dedicated/Private contracts — we can outline options in the SOW.

[11:12] (small cross-talk / laughter)

Recap & next steps:
- Redwood to share SOC 2 report, ISO notes, DPA and pilot SOW template (Action: Maya, by 2026-05-10).
- SE to deliver benchmark harness, test plan, and cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted Private (Action: Diego, by 2026-05-13).
- Customer to confirm sample dataset (anonymized) and residency constraints (Action: Sofia & Lydia, by 2026-05-12).
- Schedule in-lab runs for week of 2026-05-18 (tentative).

Closing:
[11:45] Sofia: This is helpful — if you can get the SOC 2 artifacts and bench template quickly we'll try to hit the board date.
[11:52] Maya: We'll follow up with the attachments and a formal pilot checklist. Thanks everyone.
[11:58] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: Some speaker labels auto-assigned; technical terms (model names, KV cache sizes) might be approximate.
